<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead" summary="Diagnose divergence across all models">
본훈련이 거의 끝났는데 PPO가 발산해 학습이 중단된 것을 발견했다. **아홉 모델 전부가 같은 상태가 아닌지 전수 점검해달라.** 이것이 논문 표에 들어갈 숫자의 유효성을 결정한다.

## 지금까지 확인된 사실

두 팔(`accumulate`, `mean`) 모두 시드 42로 100 에피소드 × 2000 스텝을 돌았고, MADDPG-MT만 아직 진행 중이며 나머지 여덟은 완주했다. 실패로 중단된 모델은 없다.

PPO에서 확인한 것은 다음과 같다. 100 에피소드 중 81개(`mean` 팔은 89개)에서 그래디언트 갱신이 0회였고, 밀도와 무관하게 **에피소드 1~19에서만 갱신되고 20부터 완전히 멈췄다.** `mean_loss`가 갱신 구간에서 이미 200만, 멈춘 구간에서 1600만으로 발산했다. 최종 체크포인트를 열어보니 `rest_state_dict`의 13개 텐서가 **전부 비유한값**이고 `act_state_dict`는 13개 모두 정상이다. `training_steps`가 1610에서 멈췄고 `swap_count`도 80에서 멈췄다. 즉 학습 모델이 NaN이 되었고 NaN 가드가 서빙 모델로의 전파를 막은 상태다.

총 갱신 횟수 비교는 PPO 1,610 대 TD3 66,944로 40배 차이다.

뿌리 원인으로 의심하는 것은 HPO가 PPO에 `learning_rate = 1.08e-3`을 골랐다는 것이다(PPO 통상값 3e-4의 3.6배). HPO 롤아웃이 350스텝에 학습 2회뿐이라 20만 스텝에서야 나타나는 발산을 볼 수 없다.

## 점검할 것

**1. 전수 스캔.** 두 팔 × 아홉 모델 = 18개 실행 전부에 대해 최종 체크포인트의 `act_state_dict`와 `rest_state_dict`에 비유한값이 있는지, `training_steps`와 `swap_count`가 어디서 멈췄는지, 진행 CSV의 `grad_updates_this_episode`에 0이 몇 개인지, `mean_loss`가 발산 추세인지를 표로 정리하라. **NaN까지 가지 않았지만 손실이 발산 중인 모델**이 가장 위험하다. 그런 모델은 경고도 안 뜨고 갱신도 계속되지만 정책은 망가져 있다.

**2. 발산 시점.** 발산한 모델마다 몇 번째 에피소드에서 손실이 꺾이는지 찾아라. 20만 스텝 중 어느 지점인지가 "HPO 롤아웃을 얼마나 늘려야 이걸 잡을 수 있는가"의 답이 된다.

**3. 하이퍼파라미터와의 상관.** `results/hpo/optuna_best_params.csv`의 각 모델 학습률·엔트로피 계수 등을 발산 여부와 대조하라. 발산한 모델들이 공통적으로 문헌 통상값보다 높은 값을 받았는지 확인하라. 웹 검색으로 각 알고리즘의 통상 학습률 범위를 근거와 함께 제시하라. **검증하지 못한 문헌은 절대 지어내지 마라.**

**4. Act 모델의 유효성.** PPO의 경우 Act가 깨끗하지만 그것은 에피소드 19 시점의 정책이다. 다른 모델들도 Act가 언제 마지막으로 갱신되었는지, 즉 `_best.pt`가 몇 번째 에피소드의 정책인지 확인하라. 100 에피소드를 돌았다고 적혀 있어도 실제 학습이 초반에 멈췄다면 그 사실이 표에 반영되어야 한다.

## 제약

**코드를 절대 수정하지 마라.** 읽기와 측정만 하고 보고서만 남긴다. `runs/` 아래는 **읽기만** 하라. MADDPG-MT가 아직 훈련 중이라 그 디렉터리에 쓰면 실행이 망가진다. `checkpoints/`, `results/`, `logs/`에도 쓰지 마라. SUMO를 구동할 일이 있으면 `PAPER4_SUMO_DIR=$(mktemp -d)`로 격리하라. 장시간 실행은 하지 마라.

## 산출물

`/home/imnyj/Workspace/paper4/critic/divergence_audit_20260903.md`에 한국어 산문으로 작성하라. 맨 위에 **"논문 표에 쓸 수 있는 모델과 없는 모델"** 판정을 표로 두고, 그 아래 항목별 근거와 실측치를 적어라. 마지막에 "질문" 절을 두라.

최종 메시지에는 어느 모델이 쓸 수 있고 어느 모델이 재훈련 대상인지만 간결히 요약하라.
</teammate-message>

119	# Congestion-term normalisation reference.
120	#
121	# The raw per-subchannel CBR this scenario produces is tiny -- an audit measured
122	# the weighted congestion term at 0.11 % of the mean penalty, against [0,1] for
123	# the other three, so "minimise network congestion", one of the paper's two
124	# stated objectives, was effectively absent from the reward.
125	#
126	# The cause is a scale mismatch, not a modelling error: four subchannels and a
127	# short airtime per update keep CBR far below 1 even when every vehicle
128	# transmits. Min-Max normalising against the REALISED maximum fixes the scale
129	# without touching the physical model, which is why it was chosen over reducing
130	# the subchannel count (that would delete the channel-selection dimension of the
131	# action space) or raising density (the density grid is a user decision).
132	#
133	# 0.60 is the realised ceiling, measured 2026-09-02 by saturating a single
134	# subchannel -- every vehicle granted every step at 23 dBm on channel 0 -- across
135	# the density grid, in a PROCESS-ISOLATED scenario and at the settled warm-up:
136	# peak 0.103 (d=5), 0.439 (20), 0.565 (40), 0.591 (50). It is an achievability
137	# bound on what a policy can actually cause, so a policy that saturates one
138	# channel pays ~1.0 rather than a fraction of it, and the term is commensurate
139	# with the other three.
140	#
141	# CORRECTION. This constant was first set to 0.25 on 2026-09-01 from a
142	# measurement that was wrong twice over: it ran at warm-up 350, i.e. on a network
143	# still filling and holding roughly half the vehicles it settles at, and it ran
144	# while other processes were regenerating the shared scenario files, so some of
145	# it described a network it had not asked for. Both errors pushed the ceiling
146	# down. At 0.25 the congestion term would have clipped to 1.0 through much of the
147	# high-density range -- flat gradient exactly where congestion is the thing being
148	# learned.

310	class DualModelHotSwapManager:
311	    """
312	    Manages atomic zero-downtime parameter synchronization between Act and Rest models.
313	    
314	    Guarantees:
315	    1. Safety: Strict NaN/Inf guard validates Rest model weights before transfer.
316	    2. Zero-Downtime: Fast serving thread reads Act model with minimal mutex overhead.
317	    3. Cross-Device Support: Seamless tensor copying across different GPU/CPU devices.
318	    4. Integrity: Copies all module parameters and buffers in-place.
319	    """
320	
321	    def __init__(
322	        self,
323	        act_model: nn.Module,
324	        rest_model: nn.Module,
325	        act_device: Optional[Union[str, torch.device]] = None,
326	        rest_device: Optional[Union[str, torch.device]] = None,
327	        swap_lock: Optional[threading.Lock] = None,
328	        on_swap_callback: Optional[Callable[[int], None]] = None,
329	        update_lock: Optional[threading.Lock] = None,
330	    ) -> None:
331	        self.act_model = act_model
332	        self.rest_model = rest_model
333	        # Held while the Rest weights are being mutated, so `hot_swap` can treat
334	        # "validate" and "copy" as ONE critical section. `HotSwapTrainer` passes
335	        # the same object to `BackgroundTrainer`; a standalone manager makes its
336	        # own, which is coherent only if nothing else writes Rest concurrently.
337	        self.update_lock = update_lock or threading.Lock()
338	        self.act_device = (
339	            torch.device(act_device)
340	            if act_device is not None
341	            else next(act_model.parameters()).device
342	            if list(act_model.parameters())
343	            else torch.device("cpu")
344	        )
345	        self.rest_device = (
346	            torch.device(rest_device)
347	            if rest_device is not None
348	            else next(rest_model.parameters()).device
349	            if list(rest_model.parameters())
350	            else torch.device("cpu")
351	        )
352	
353	        self.swap_lock = swap_lock if swap_lock is not None else threading.Lock()
354	        self.on_swap_callback = on_swap_callback
355	
356	        self.swap_count = 0
357	        self.failed_swaps = 0
358	        self.last_swap_time = 0.0
359	        self.swap_latencies_ms: List[float] = []
360	
361	    def validate_weights(self) -> bool:
362	        """
363	        Validates all parameters and buffers in Rest model against NaN and Inf.
364	        Returns True if all tensors are clean and finite, False otherwise.
365	        """
366	        for name, p in self.rest_model.named_parameters():
367	            if torch.isnan(p).any() or torch.isinf(p).any():
368	                return False
369	        for name, b in self.rest_model.named_buffers():
370	            if torch.isnan(b).any() or torch.isinf(b).any():
371	                return False
372	        return True
373	
374	    def hot_swap(self) -> bool:
375	        """
376	        Atomically copies Rest model parameters & buffers into Act model in-place.
377	        
378	        Returns:
379	            bool: True if hot-swap succeeded, False if rejected by safety guard.
380	        """
381	        # The NaN guard is only sound if nothing can write Rest between the
382	        # check and the copy. It used to validate OUTSIDE any lock and then take
383	        # `swap_lock` to copy, so a gradient step landing in that window put the
384	        # NaNs it had just produced straight into the Act model -- past a guard
385	        # that had already said "clean". `validate_weights` could also read a
386	        # half-written tensor and pass on a value that never existed. Both halves
387	        # now run under `update_lock`, which `BackgroundTrainer.train_step` holds
388	        # across `rest_model.update()`.
389	        #
390	        # Lock order is `update_lock` -> `swap_lock` everywhere (here and in
391	        # `HotSwapTrainer.save_checkpoint`); `train_step` releases `update_lock`
392	        # before it can reach this method, so no inversion is possible.
393	        t0 = time.perf_counter()
394	        with self.update_lock:
395	            # 1. NaN / Inf Safety Guard
396	            if not self.validate_weights():
397	                self.failed_swaps += 1
398	                return False
399	
400	            # 2. Atomic In-Place Parameter Transfer under Mutex
401	            with self.swap_lock:
402	                with torch.no_grad():
403	                    # Copy parameters
404	                    for p_act, p_rest in zip(self.act_model.parameters(), self.rest_model.parameters()):
405	                        if p_act.device == p_rest.device:
406	                            p_act.data.copy_(p_rest.data)
407	                        else:
408	                            p_act.data.copy_(p_rest.data.to(p_act.device))
409	
410	                    # Copy named buffers (e.g., running stats)
411	                    for b_act, b_rest in zip(self.act_model.buffers(), self.rest_model.buffers()):
412	                        if b_act.device == b_rest.device:
413	                            b_act.data.copy_(b_rest.data)
414	                        else:
415	                            b_act.data.copy_(b_rest.data.to(b_act.device))
416	
417	        latency_ms = (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000.0
418	        self.swap_latencies_ms.append(latency_ms)
419	        self.swap_count += 1
420	        self.last_swap_time = time.time()
421	
422	        if self.on_swap_callback is not None:
423	            try:
424	                self.on_swap_callback(self.swap_count)
425	            except Exception:
426	                pass
427	
428	        return True
429	
430	    def get_stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
431	        """Returns hot-swap execution statistics."""
432	        mean_lat = float(np.mean(self.swap_latencies_ms)) if self.swap_latencies_ms else 0.0
433	        max_lat = float(np.max(self.swap_latencies_ms)) if self.swap_latencies_ms else 0.0
434	        return {
435	            "swap_count": self.swap_count,
436	            "failed_swaps": self.failed_swaps,
437	            "last_swap_time": self.last_swap_time,
438	            "mean_swap_latency_ms": round(mean_lat, 4),
439	            "max_swap_latency_ms": round(max_lat, 4),
440	        }

443	class TransitionStreamer:
444	    """
445	    Thread-safe non-blocking queue for streaming transition tuples from simulation to trainer.
446	    """
447	
448	    def __init__(self, maxsize: int = 20000) -> None:
449	        self.maxsize = int(maxsize)
450	        self.queue: queue.Queue = queue.Queue(maxsize=self.maxsize)
451	        self.pushed_count = 0
452	        self.dropped_count = 0
453	        self.drained_count = 0
454	
455	    def push(
456	        self,
457	        state: Union[np.ndarray, List[float]],
458	        action: Union[np.ndarray, List[float], Tuple[float, ...]],
459	        reward: float,
460	        next_state: Union[np.ndarray, List[float]],
461	        done: bool,
462	        delta_t: float,
463	        action_idx: Optional[int] = None,
464	    ) -> bool:
465	        """
466	        Non-blocking transition push. Drops item if queue is full to preserve simulation speed.
467	
468	        `action_idx` is the COMBINED DISCRETE ACTION INDEX the policy's discrete
469	        head actually selected, when it has one. `RetrospectiveReplayBuffer.push`
470	        has accepted it since it was written, but this streamer had no such
471	        parameter, `push_to_buffer` pulled six fixed keys out of the item dict,
472	        and `HotSwapRLScheduler.decide_grant` threw away the `info` dict that
473	        carries it -- so the index never survived the trip from the model to the
474	        buffer. Measured consequence: `action_idx` was absent from the sampled
475	        batch for all nine baselines, and the five discrete-head models
476	        (SPAM-D3QN, CARLTON, MA2HDQN, I-HAMAPPO, RES-MAPDDPG) all fell back to
477	        re-deriving the index from the decoded continuous action, which is lossy
478	        and lossy by a DIFFERENT amount per model -- so the nine were not being
479	        compared under the same conditions.
480	        """
481	        item = {
482	            "state": state,
483	            "action": action,
484	            "reward": float(reward),
485	            "next_state": next_state,
486	            "done": bool(done),
487	            "delta_t": float(delta_t),
488	            "action_idx": None if action_idx is None else int(action_idx),
489	        }
490	        try:
491	            self.queue.put_nowait(item)
492	            self.pushed_count += 1
493	            return True
494	        except queue.Full:
495	            self.dropped_count += 1
496	            return False
497	
498	    def drain(self, max_items: Optional[int] = None) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
499	        """Drains pending transitions from queue without blocking."""
500	        items: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
501	        limit = max_items if max_items is not None else self.queue.qsize() + 100
502	        for _ in range(limit):
503	            try:
504	                item = self.queue.get_nowait()
505	                items.append(item)
506	                self.queue.task_done()
507	            except queue.Empty:
508	                break
509	        self.drained_count += len(items)
510	        return items
511	
512	    def push_to_buffer(self, replay_buffer: RetrospectiveReplayBuffer, max_items: Optional[int] = None) -> int:
513	        """Drains transitions from queue and directly inserts into replay buffer."""
514	        items = self.drain(max_items=max_items)
515	        for it in items:
516	            replay_buffer.push(
517	                state=it["state"],
518	                action=it["action"],
519	                reward=it["reward"],
520	                next_state=it["next_state"],
521	                done=it["done"],
522	                delta_t=it["delta_t"],
523	                action_idx=it.get("action_idx"),
524	            )
525	        return len(items)
526	
527	    def qsize(self) -> int:
528	        return self.queue.qsize()
529	
530	    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
531	        return self.queue.empty()
532	
533	    def clear(self) -> None:
534	        self.drain()
535	        self.pushed_count = 0
536	        self.dropped_count = 0
537	        self.drained_count = 0

542	    Dedicated background training worker that consumes transitions from ReplayBuffer,
543	    performs gradient updates on Rest model, and triggers periodic atomic hot-swaps.
544	    """
545	
546	    def __init__(
547	        self,
548	        rest_model: nn.Module,
549	        replay_buffer: RetrospectiveReplayBuffer,
550	        streamer: TransitionStreamer,
551	        hot_swap_manager: DualModelHotSwapManager,
552	        batch_size: int = 32,
553	        train_frequency: int = 1,
554	        swap_interval_steps: int = 20,
555	        rest_device: Optional[torch.device] = None,
556	        loss_history_maxlen: int = 1000,
557	    ) -> None:
558	        self.rest_model = rest_model
559	        self.replay_buffer = replay_buffer
560	        self.streamer = streamer
561	        self.hot_swap_manager = hot_swap_manager
562	        self.batch_size = int(batch_size)
563	        # `train_frequency` is the gradient-updates-per-environment-step ratio.
564	        # It exists because the background worker otherwise spins as fast as the
565	        # wall clock allows, so a cheap model gets many more updates than an
566	        # expensive one over the same episode -- measured 18x across the density
567	        # schedule. In a comparison paper that is a confound: a baseline could
568	        # lose because it was handed less training, not because it is worse.
569	        # `updates_allowed()` caps the worker at `train_frequency * env_steps`;
570	        # the cap only ever SLOWS the fast models, never speeds up the slow ones,
571	        # so no model is ever given less than it would have had.
572	        self.train_frequency = float(train_frequency)
573	        # Set by the training loop as the environment advances. None disables the
574	        # cap entirely, which is the historical (wall-clock) behaviour.
575	        self.env_steps_seen: Optional[int] = None
576	        self.swap_interval_steps = int(swap_interval_steps)
577	        self.rest_device = rest_device or (
578	            next(rest_model.parameters()).device if list(rest_model.parameters()) else torch.device("cpu")
579	        )
580	
581	        self.worker_thread: Optional[threading.Thread] = None
582	        self.stop_event = threading.Event()
583	        self.training_steps = 0
584	        # A Rest model that diverges to NaN fails `validate_weights()` and the
585	        # swap is refused, which FREEZES the Act model on its last good weights.
586	        # The simulation keeps running, the metrics stay plausible, and the
587	        # reward curve actually looks *more* stable because the policy stopped
588	        # changing -- so an 8.8 hour run could burn to completion before anyone
589	        # saw `failed_swaps` in the final summary. These two make it observable
590	        # while the run is still alive, and `fatal_error` lets the episode loop
591	        # abort instead of finishing a run that is training nothing.
592	        self.consecutive_failed_swaps = 0
593	        self.max_consecutive_failed_swaps = max(10, int(self.swap_interval_steps) * 10)
594	        self.fatal_error: Optional[str] = None
595	        # Held while the Rest model's weights are being mutated by `update()`, so
596	        # a checkpoint writer can obtain a quiescent snapshot. Distinct from
597	        # `self.lock` (bookkeeping) and from `swap_lock` (Act <- Rest transfer):
598	        # `update()` deliberately runs OUTSIDE `self.lock` to keep the swap
599	        # cadence off the gradient path, which left the Rest weights mutating
600	        # under any concurrent reader. See HotSwapTrainer.save_checkpoint.
601	        # The manager owns this: `hot_swap()` needs the same lock to make its
602	        # NaN guard and its copy one critical section.
603	        self.update_lock = self.hot_swap_manager.update_lock
604	        # Bounded ring buffer: over a 200,000-step run an unbounded list would grow
605	        # without limit while only the last 50 entries are ever read.
606	        self.loss_history_maxlen = int(loss_history_maxlen)
607	        self.loss_history: Deque[Dict[str, float]] = deque(maxlen=self.loss_history_maxlen)
608	        self.lock = threading.Lock()
609	
610	    def train_step(self) -> Optional[Dict[str, float]]:
611	        """
612	        Executes one gradient update step on Rest model and performs hot-swap if scheduled.
613	        """
614	        # Drain any pending transitions into replay buffer
615	        self.streamer.push_to_buffer(self.replay_buffer)
616	
617	        if not self.replay_buffer.is_ready(self.batch_size):
618	            return None
619	
620	        if not self.updates_allowed():
621	            return None
622	
623	        batch = self.replay_buffer.sample(self.batch_size)
624

754	        """Run the Act model on an observation the ENVIRONMENT produced.
755	
756	        This method is pure inference. It used to also (a) build its own state
757	        vector from a partial dict and (b) compute its own three-term reward,
758	        which is what the replay buffer was actually trained on. Both are gone:
759	
760	          (a) it re-vectorised from `{vid, current_time, pos, speed}`, so 15 of
761	              the 18 dimensions fell back to defaults and reached the model as
762	              constants -- traffic light, distance to RSU, CBR, heading, age.
763	              The rich vector the environment builds was discarded by the caller.
764	          (b) its reward was `-(0.1*dt + 1.0*err + 0.01*power)` with `err`
765	              permanently 0 (the key was never passed) and `dt` permanently 0.1,
766	              i.e. the only live training signal in the whole pipeline was
767	              transmit power. The approved four-term reward went to the log file.

769	        Both now have exactly one owner, the environment (design_spec_v2 P1/P2).
770	
771	        Returns `(grant, raw_action, action_idx)`. The caller stores the last two
772	        so the transition can be pushed with the action the policy actually
773	        emitted AND with the discrete index its discrete head actually chose.
774

776	        returns `(grant, raw_action, info)` and `info["action_idx"]` is where the
777	        five discrete-head baselines report their argmax, so discarding it forced
778	        every one of them onto a lossy reconstruction path.

780	        s = np.asarray(state_vec, dtype=np.float32)
781	        assert s.shape == (self.state_dim,), (
782	            f"FATAL: observation for {vid} has width {s.shape}, expected ({self.state_dim},). "
783	            "The environment is the only legitimate source of observations."
784	        )

786	        t0 = time.perf_counter()

788	        with self.hot_swap_manager.swap_lock:
789	            grant, raw_action, info = self.act_model.select_action(s, deterministic=False)

795	        if isinstance(info, dict):
796	            raw_idx = info.get("action_idx")

800	                except (TypeError, ValueError):
801	                    action_idx = None

805	        self,

982	        constructor in the MRO named it, and it therefore had no effect" -- it

# src/hot_swap_trainer.py
# ============================================================================
# Dual-Model Hot-Swap Training Pipeline (S4 / R4)
#
# Implements:
# 1. DualModelHotSwapManager: Zero-downtime atomic hot-swap manager with
#    strict NaN/Inf validation, cross-device support, and thread-safe mutex.
# 2. TransitionStreamer: High-throughput non-blocking thread-safe queue
#    streaming transitions from simulation/serving steps to background trainer.
# 3. BackgroundTrainer: Dedicated background training worker executing
#    gradient updates on Rest model and triggering periodic hot-swaps.
# 4. HotSwapRLScheduler: Act-model inference and transition forwarding. It does
#    NOT build observations or price rewards -- see design_spec_v2 principle P1.
# 5. HotSwapTrainer: Master orchestrator for Act/Rest model lifecycle.
# 6. AoiV2IEnv: Genuine SUMO environment integration with 4 anti-mocking
#    assertions. Sole owner of the observation vector and the reward function.
# 7. run_hot_swap_training: Full end-to-end training loop execution function
#    supporting 200,000 steps, TensorBoard logging, and checkpointing.
#
# The loop is EVENT-DRIVEN, not a gym rollout: each vehicle has its own decision
# epochs spaced by the Delta the policy chose for it, so there is no single
# global (s, a, r, s') tick. A grant fires when the clock reaches its deadline,
# not on the step it was issued. See design_spec_v2.md sections 1, 5 and 9.

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reward weights are a property of the BENCHMARK, not of any single model.
# Training (`run_hot_swap_training`), evaluation (`src/evaluate.py`) and the
# hyper-parameter search (`src/hpo.py`) all read these same four numbers, so
# every baseline is optimised and scored against one identical reward. Tuning
# them per model would give each baseline a different objective and make the
# cross-model comparison in the paper meaningless.
#
# They are also the reason `HotSwapTrainer` filters them out of `hparams`:
# w1..w4 are `AoiV2IEnv.__init__` arguments, and every baseline constructor
# ends in `**hparams`, so a stray `w1` would be silently swallowed by the model
# and never reach the reward at all.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
REWARD_WEIGHT_KEYS: Tuple[str, ...] = ("w1", "w2", "w3", "w4")

DEFAULT_REWARD_WEIGHTS: Dict[str, float] = {
    "w1": 0.5,   # normalised squared estimation error
    "w2": 0.2,   # transmit power
    "w3": 0.2,   # channel congestion

# Raw (un-normalised) Optuna samples for the weights above. They are recorded in
# the HPO CSV for provenance and must never be forwarded to a model either.
RAW_REWARD_WEIGHT_KEYS: Tuple[str, ...] = tuple(f"{k}_raw" for k in REWARD_WEIGHT_KEYS)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Congestion-term normalisation reference.
#
# The raw per-subchannel CBR this scenario produces is tiny -- an audit measured
# the weighted congestion term at 0.11 % of the mean penalty, against [0,1] for
# the other three, so "minimise network congestion", one of the paper's two
# stated objectives, was effectively absent from the reward.
#
# The cause is a scale mismatch, not a modelling error: four subchannels and a
# short airtime per update keep CBR far below 1 even when every vehicle
# transmits. Min-Max normalising against the REALISED maximum fixes the scale
# without touching the physical model, which is why it was chosen over reducing
# the subchannel count (that would delete the channel-selection dimension of the
# action space) or raising density (the density grid is a user decision).
#
# 0.60 is the realised ceiling, measured 2026-09-02 by saturating a single
# subchannel -- every vehicle granted every step at 23 dBm on channel 0 -- across
# the density grid, in a PROCESS-ISOLATED scenario and at the settled warm-up:
# peak 0.103 (d=5), 0.439 (20), 0.565 (40), 0.591 (50). It is an achievability
# bound on what a policy can actually cause, so a policy that saturates one
# channel pays ~1.0 rather than a fraction of it, and the term is commensurate
# with the other three.
#
# CORRECTION. This constant was first set to 0.25 on 2026-09-01 from a
# measurement that was wrong twice over: it ran at warm-up 350, i.e. on a network
# still filling and holding roughly half the vehicles it settles at, and it ran
# while other processes were regenerating the shared scenario files, so some of
# it described a network it had not asked for. Both errors pushed the ceiling
# down. At 0.25 the congestion term would have clipped to 1.0 through much of the
# high-density range -- flat gradient exactly where congestion is the thing being
# learned.
CBR_REF: float = 0.60

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Warm-up: how long SUMO runs before the episode starts measuring.
#
# 350 steps (35 s) was chosen when the only requirement was "some vehicle has
# reached the RSU disc". It does not get the network anywhere near loaded.
# Measured 2026-09-02, in-range vehicle count by step: density 25 climbs 26 ->
# 46 -> 67 -> 87 -> 93, and the second half of a 1200-step window averages 1.70x
# the first. Density 10 settles around step 800, density 50 around step 1200.
#
# Measuring a network that is still filling makes the density axis of the results
# table mean something other than what it says: at warm-up 350 a "density 25"
# episode sees 47 vehicles in range where the settled value is 119. Comparisons
# ACROSS densities would then be partly comparisons of how much transient each
# one happened to include, which is not a property of the scheduling policy.
#
# The cost is real and was measured: the settled network holds ~2.5x the
# vehicles, so a measured step goes from 7.2 ms to 28 ms, roughly 4x the run
# time. That is the price of the density axis meaning what it claims.
DEFAULT_WARMUP_STEPS: int = 1200

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# How the error term aggregates over an SMDP interval.
#
# The two governing documents disagree. `design_spec_v2` D2 defines R_k with the
# error term ACCUMULATED across the interval (an integral, so a long Delta pays
# proportionally more), while `Conversation.md` section 3 requires all four terms
# normalised to [0,1] (which makes it an interval MEAN). Measured split under
# "accumulate": error 82.1 %, power 9.7 %, redundancy 8.0 %, congestion 0.11 %,
# with raw r_err reaching 38.35 against 1.0 for the others.
#
# Neither is obviously right. Accumulation is the honest SMDP integral and keeps
# pressure on long silent gaps, which is the paper's core claim; averaging makes
# the four terms commensurate so the power and redundancy penalties actually
# steer behaviour. The user's decision was to run BOTH and compare, so this is a
# switch rather than a fix, and the mode is recorded in every checkpoint and
# results row so no number is ever ambiguous about which reward produced it.
ERROR_MODE_ACCUMULATE = "accumulate"   # design_spec_v2 D2: integral over the interval
ERROR_MODE_MEAN = "mean"               # Conversation.md section 3: interval average, [0,1]
REWARD_ERROR_MODES: Tuple[str, ...] = (ERROR_MODE_ACCUMULATE, ERROR_MODE_MEAN)
DEFAULT_ERROR_MODE: str = ERROR_MODE_ACCUMULATE

# Every key here belongs to the environment or the benchmark, never to a model
# constructor. Kept as an exported name (`run_all.py` imports it) and as the
# *reward-weight* subset; the full environment key set is resolved from
# `AoiV2IEnv.__init__` itself by `env_param_names()` below.
ENV_ONLY_HPARAM_KEYS: frozenset = frozenset(REWARD_WEIGHT_KEYS + RAW_REWARD_WEIGHT_KEYS)


def env_param_names() -> frozenset:
    """Named parameters of `AoiV2IEnv.__init__`, resolved from the signature.

    This is the POSITIVE half of the hyper-parameter routing. The previous
    blacklist listed eight literal keys (`w1..w4`, `w1_raw..w4_raw`) and every
    other environment argument leaked straight into the model constructor, where
    the `**hparams` tail swallowed it in silence. Measured on the real classes:
    `density=55.0`, `warmup_steps=9` and even `total_nonsense=1` were accepted
    without a word by SPAMD3QN, PPO and CARLTON, so a CSV column named `density`
    would have trained the whole benchmark at the default 25.0 while the log
    claimed otherwise. Reading the signature means new environment arguments are
    routed correctly the day they are added.
    """
    sig = inspect.signature(AoiV2IEnv.__init__)
    return frozenset(
        name for name, prm in sig.parameters.items()
        if name != "self" and prm.kind in (prm.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD, prm.KEYWORD_ONLY)
    )


def split_env_hparams(hparams: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Split a flat hparams dict into (model kwargs, environment-only kwargs).

    Routing is by `AoiV2IEnv.__init__`'s own signature plus the raw Optuna
    provenance columns (`w1_raw`..`w4_raw`), which belong to neither side and are
    recorded only so a CSV row can be traced back to its trial.

    Anything the environment does not name is handed to the model, and
    `HotSwapTrainer` then verifies the model actually CONSUMED it (see
    `_assert_model_consumed_hparams`) rather than swallowing it.
    """
    env_names = env_param_names() | set(RAW_REWARD_WEIGHT_KEYS)
    model_hparams: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    env_hparams: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    for key, value in (hparams or {}).items():
        if key in env_names:
            env_hparams[key] = value
        else:
            model_hparams[key] = value
    return model_hparams, env_hparams

def infer_state_dim(vectorizer: Optional[StateVectorizer] = None) -> int:
    """
    Resolves the observation vector dimension from `StateVectorizer` itself.

    The state layout is owned by `src/rl_interface.py::StateVectorizer`; this
    module must never hardcode it (it grew from 16 to 18 dims when `n_queue`
    and `heading` were added). Resolution order:
      1. an explicit dimension attribute exposed by the vectorizer, if any;
      2. otherwise probe the real vectorizer with an empty state dict and
         measure the length of the vector it actually produces.

    Returns the measured dimension; never guesses a literal unless both the
    attribute and the probe are unavailable.
    """
    vec = vectorizer if vectorizer is not None else StateVectorizer()
    for attr in ("STATE_DIM", "state_dim", "dim", "n_features", "num_features"):
        val = getattr(vec, attr, None)
        if callable(val):
            try:
                val = val()
            except Exception:
                val = None
        if isinstance(val, (int, np.integer)) and int(val) > 0:
            return int(val)
    try:
        return int(len(vec.vectorize_from_dict({}, (0.0, 0.0))))
    except Exception:
        # Last-resort fallback: the canonical design dimension (Conversation.md
        # section 1: 16 base features + n_queue + heading).
        # Last resort. Import the canonical width rather than restating it: a
        # literal here silently disagreed with STATE_DIM when the vector went
        # from 18 to 17 dimensions.
        from src.rl_interface import STATE_DIM as _CANONICAL_STATE_DIM

def select_default_devices() -> Tuple[torch.device, torch.device]:
    """
    Selects optimal PyTorch devices for Act and Rest models based on available hardware.
    
    Returns:
        (act_device, rest_device)
        - Multi-GPU (>=2 GPUs): Act on cuda:0, Rest on cuda:1 (Complete hardware isolation)
        - Single GPU: Act on cuda:0, Rest on cuda:0
        - CPU: Act on cpu, Rest on cpu
    """
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        num_devices = torch.cuda.device_count()
        act_device = torch.device("cuda:0")
        if num_devices >= 2:
            rest_device = torch.device("cuda:1")
        else:
            rest_device = torch.device("cuda:0")
    else:
        act_device = torch.device("cpu")
        rest_device = torch.device("cpu")
    return act_device, rest_device


class DualModelHotSwapManager:
    """
    Manages atomic zero-downtime parameter synchronization between Act and Rest models.
    
    Guarantees:
    1. Safety: Strict NaN/Inf guard validates Rest model weights before transfer.
    2. Zero-Downtime: Fast serving thread reads Act model with minimal mutex overhead.
    3. Cross-Device Support: Seamless tensor copying across different GPU/CPU devices.
    4. Integrity: Copies all module parameters and buffers in-place.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        act_model: nn.Module,
        rest_model: nn.Module,
        act_device: Optional[Union[str, torch.device]] = None,
        rest_device: Optional[Union[str, torch.device]] = None,
        swap_lock: Optional[threading.Lock] = None,
        on_swap_callback: Optional[Callable[[int], None]] = None,
        update_lock: Optional[threading.Lock] = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.act_model = act_model
        self.rest_model = rest_model
        # Held while the Rest weights are being mutated, so `hot_swap` can treat
        # "validate" and "copy" as ONE critical section. `HotSwapTrainer` passes
        # the same object to `BackgroundTrainer`; a standalone manager makes its
        # own, which is coherent only if nothing else writes Rest concurrently.
        self.update_lock = update_lock or threading.Lock()
        self.act_device = (
            torch.device(act_device)
            if act_device is not None
            else next(act_model.parameters()).device
            if list(act_model.parameters())
            else torch.device("cpu")
        )
        self.rest_device = (
            torch.device(rest_device)
            if rest_device is not None
            else next(rest_model.parameters()).device
            if list(rest_model.parameters())
            else torch.device("cpu")
        )

        self.swap_lock = swap_lock if swap_lock is not None else threading.Lock()
        self.on_swap_callback = on_swap_callback

        self.swap_count = 0
        self.failed_swaps = 0
        self.last_swap_time = 0.0
        self.swap_latencies_ms: List[float] = []

    def validate_weights(self) -> bool:
        """
        Validates all parameters and buffers in Rest model against NaN and Inf.
        Returns True if all tensors are clean and finite, False otherwise.
        """
        for name, p in self.rest_model.named_parameters():
            if torch.isnan(p).any() or torch.isinf(p).any():
                return False
        for name, b in self.rest_model.named_buffers():
            if torch.isnan(b).any() or torch.isinf(b).any():
                return False
        return True

    def hot_swap(self) -> bool:
        """
        Atomically copies Rest model parameters & buffers into Act model in-place.
        
        Returns:
            bool: True if hot-swap succeeded, False if rejected by safety guard.
        """
        # The NaN guard is only sound if nothing can write Rest between the
        # check and the copy. It used to validate OUTSIDE any lock and then take
        # `swap_lock` to copy, so a gradient step landing in that window put the
        # NaNs it had just produced straight into the Act model -- past a guard
        # that had already said "clean". `validate_weights` could also read a
        # half-written tensor and pass on a value that never existed. Both halves
        # now run under `update_lock`, which `BackgroundTrainer.train_step` holds
        # across `rest_model.update()`.
        #
        # Lock order is `update_lock` -> `swap_lock` everywhere (here and in
        # `HotSwapTrainer.save_checkpoint`); `train_step` releases `update_lock`
        # before it can reach this method, so no inversion is possible.
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        with self.update_lock:
            # 1. NaN / Inf Safety Guard
            if not self.validate_weights():
                self.failed_swaps += 1
                return False

            # 2. Atomic In-Place Parameter Transfer under Mutex
            with self.swap_lock:
                with torch.no_grad():
                    # Copy parameters
                    for p_act, p_rest in zip(self.act_model.parameters(), self.rest_model.parameters()):
                        if p_act.device == p_rest.device:
                            p_act.data.copy_(p_rest.data)
                        else:
                            p_act.data.copy_(p_rest.data.to(p_act.device))

                    # Copy named buffers (e.g., running stats)
                    for b_act, b_rest in zip(self.act_model.buffers(), self.rest_model.buffers()):
                        if b_act.device == b_rest.device:
                            b_act.data.copy_(b_rest.data)
                        else:
                            b_act.data.copy_(b_rest.data.to(b_act.device))

        latency_ms = (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000.0
        self.swap_latencies_ms.append(latency_ms)
        self.swap_count += 1
        self.last_swap_time = time.time()

        if self.on_swap_callback is not None:
            try:
                self.on_swap_callback(self.swap_count)
            except Exception:
                pass

        return True

    def get_stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Returns hot-swap execution statistics."""
        mean_lat = float(np.mean(self.swap_latencies_ms)) if self.swap_latencies_ms else 0.0
        max_lat = float(np.max(self.swap_latencies_ms)) if self.swap_latencies_ms else 0.0
        return {
            "swap_count": self.swap_count,
            "failed_swaps": self.failed_swaps,
            "last_swap_time": self.last_swap_time,
            "mean_swap_latency_ms": round(mean_lat, 4),
            "max_swap_latency_ms": round(max_lat, 4),
        }


class TransitionStreamer:
    """
    Thread-safe non-blocking queue for streaming transition tuples from simulation to trainer.
    """

    def __init__(self, maxsize: int = 20000) -> None:
        self.maxsize = int(maxsize)
        self.queue: queue.Queue = queue.Queue(maxsize=self.maxsize)
        self.pushed_count = 0
        self.dropped_count = 0
        self.drained_count = 0

    def push(
        self,
        state: Union[np.ndarray, List[float]],
        action: Union[np.ndarray, List[float], Tuple[float, ...]],
        reward: float,
        next_state: Union[np.ndarray, List[float]],
        done: bool,
        delta_t: float,
        action_idx: Optional[int] = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """
        Non-blocking transition push. Drops item if queue is full to preserve simulation speed.

        `action_idx` is the COMBINED DISCRETE ACTION INDEX the policy's discrete
        head actually selected, when it has one. `RetrospectiveReplayBuffer.push`
        has accepted it since it was written, but this streamer had no such
        parameter, `push_to_buffer` pulled six fixed keys out of the item dict,
        and `HotSwapRLScheduler.decide_grant` threw away the `info` dict that
        carries it -- so the index never survived the trip from the model to the
        buffer. Measured consequence: `action_idx` was absent from the sampled
        batch for all nine baselines, and the five discrete-head models
        (SPAM-D3QN, CARLTON, MA2HDQN, I-HAMAPPO, RES-MAPDDPG) all fell back to
        re-deriving the index from the decoded continuous action, which is lossy
        and lossy by a DIFFERENT amount per model -- so the nine were not being
        compared under the same conditions.
        """
        item = {
            "state": state,
            "action": action,
            "reward": float(reward),
            "next_state": next_state,
            "done": bool(done),
            "delta_t": float(delta_t),
            "action_idx": None if action_idx is None else int(action_idx),
        }
        try:
            self.queue.put_nowait(item)
            self.pushed_count += 1
            return True
        except queue.Full:
            self.dropped_count += 1
            return False

    def drain(self, max_items: Optional[int] = None) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Drains pending transitions from queue without blocking."""
        items: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        limit = max_items if max_items is not None else self.queue.qsize() + 100
        for _ in range(limit):
            try:
                item = self.queue.get_nowait()
                items.append(item)
                self.queue.task_done()
            except queue.Empty:
                break
        self.drained_count += len(items)
        return items

    def push_to_buffer(self, replay_buffer: RetrospectiveReplayBuffer, max_items: Optional[int] = None) -> int:
        """Drains transitions from queue and directly inserts into replay buffer."""
        items = self.drain(max_items=max_items)
        for it in items:
            replay_buffer.push(
                state=it["state"],
                action=it["action"],
                reward=it["reward"],
                next_state=it["next_state"],
                done=it["done"],
                delta_t=it["delta_t"],
                action_idx=it.get("action_idx"),
            )
        return len(items)

    def qsize(self) -> int:
        return self.queue.qsize()

    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
        return self.queue.empty()

    def clear(self) -> None:
        self.drain()
        self.pushed_count = 0
        self.dropped_count = 0
        self.drained_count = 0


class BackgroundTrainer:
    """
    Dedicated background training worker that consumes transitions from ReplayBuffer,
    performs gradient updates on Rest model, and triggers periodic atomic hot-swaps.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        rest_model: nn.Module,
        replay_buffer: RetrospectiveReplayBuffer,
        streamer: TransitionStreamer,
        hot_swap_manager: DualModelHotSwapManager,
        batch_size: int = 32,
        train_frequency: int = 1,
        swap_interval_steps: int = 20,
        rest_device: Optional[torch.device] = None,
        loss_history_maxlen: int = 1000,
    ) -> None:
        self.rest_model = rest_model
        self.replay_buffer = replay_buffer
        self.streamer = streamer
        self.hot_swap_manager = hot_swap_manager
        self.batch_size = int(batch_size)
        # `train_frequency` is the gradient-updates-per-environment-step ratio.
        # It exists because the background worker otherwise spins as fast as the
        # wall clock allows, so a cheap model gets many more updates than an
        # expensive one over the same episode -- measured 18x across the density
        # schedule. In a comparison paper that is a confound: a baseline could
        # lose because it was handed less training, not because it is worse.
        # `updates_allowed()` caps the worker at `train_frequency * env_steps`;
        # the cap only ever SLOWS the fast models, never speeds up the slow ones,
        # so no model is ever given less than it would have had.
        self.train_frequency = float(train_frequency)
        # Set by the training loop as the environment advances. None disables the
        # cap entirely, which is the historical (wall-clock) behaviour.
        self.env_steps_seen: Optional[int] = None
        self.swap_interval_steps = int(swap_interval_steps)
        self.rest_device = rest_device or (
            next(rest_model.parameters()).device if list(rest_model.parameters()) else torch.device("cpu")
        )

        self.worker_thread: Optional[threading.Thread] = None
        self.stop_event = threading.Event()
        self.training_steps = 0
        # A Rest model that diverges to NaN fails `validate_weights()` and the
        # swap is refused, which FREEZES the Act model on its last good weights.
        # The simulation keeps running, the metrics stay plausible, and the
        # reward curve actually looks *more* stable because the policy stopped
        # changing -- so an 8.8 hour run could burn to completion before anyone
        # saw `failed_swaps` in the final summary. These two make it observable
        # while the run is still alive, and `fatal_error` lets the episode loop
        # abort instead of finishing a run that is training nothing.
        self.consecutive_failed_swaps = 0
        self.max_consecutive_failed_swaps = max(10, int(self.swap_interval_steps) * 10)
        self.fatal_error: Optional[str] = None
        # Held while the Rest model's weights are being mutated by `update()`, so
        # a checkpoint writer can obtain a quiescent snapshot. Distinct from
        # `self.lock` (bookkeeping) and from `swap_lock` (Act <- Rest transfer):
        # `update()` deliberately runs OUTSIDE `self.lock` to keep the swap
        # cadence off the gradient path, which left the Rest weights mutating
        # under any concurrent reader. See HotSwapTrainer.save_checkpoint.
        # The manager owns this: `hot_swap()` needs the same lock to make its
        # NaN guard and its copy one critical section.
        self.update_lock = self.hot_swap_manager.update_lock
        # Bounded ring buffer: over a 200,000-step run an unbounded list would grow
        # without limit while only the last 50 entries are ever read.
        self.loss_history_maxlen = int(loss_history_maxlen)
        self.loss_history: Deque[Dict[str, float]] = deque(maxlen=self.loss_history_maxlen)
        self.lock = threading.Lock()

    def train_step(self) -> Optional[Dict[str, float]]:
        """
        Executes one gradient update step on Rest model and performs hot-swap if scheduled.
        """
        # Drain any pending transitions into replay buffer
        self.streamer.push_to_buffer(self.replay_buffer)

        if not self.replay_buffer.is_ready(self.batch_size):
            return None

        if not self.updates_allowed():
            return None

        batch = self.replay_buffer.sample(self.batch_size)

        # Move batch tensors to Rest model's device
        if self.rest_device is not None:
            batch = {k: v.to(self.rest_device) if isinstance(v, torch.Tensor) else v for k, v in batch.items()}

        self.rest_model.train()
        with self.update_lock:
            loss_dict = self.rest_model.update(batch)

        with self.lock:
            self.training_steps += 1
            self.loss_history.append(loss_dict)

            # Scheduled Hot-swap
            if self.training_steps % self.swap_interval_steps == 0:
                swapped = self.hot_swap_manager.hot_swap()
                if swapped:
                    self.consecutive_failed_swaps = 0
                else:
                    self.consecutive_failed_swaps += 1
                    logging.error(
                        "Hot-swap REFUSED (NaN/Inf in Rest weights). "
                        "Consecutive failures: %d/%d. The Act model is frozen on its "
                        "last valid weights and is no longer learning.",
                        self.consecutive_failed_swaps, self.max_consecutive_failed_swaps,
                    )
                    if self.consecutive_failed_swaps >= self.max_consecutive_failed_swaps:
                        self.fatal_error = (
                            f"{self.consecutive_failed_swaps} consecutive hot-swaps refused: "
                            "the Rest model has diverged and the Act model is frozen. "
                            "Continuing would burn the remaining wall-clock on a policy "
                            "that cannot change."
                        )

        return loss_dict

    def updates_allowed(self) -> bool:
        """True while this model is still under its env-step-linked update budget.

        Returns True unconditionally when `env_steps_seen` is None, which is the
        wall-clock behaviour every result before 2026-09-01 was produced under.
        """
        if self.env_steps_seen is None:
            return True
        budget = self.train_frequency * float(self.env_steps_seen)
        return float(self.training_steps) < budget

    def _worker_loop(self) -> None:
        """Background thread execution loop."""
        while not self.stop_event.is_set():
            loss_dict = self.train_step()
            if loss_dict is None:
                time.sleep(0.002)
            else:
                time.sleep(0.0005)

    def start(self) -> None:
        """Starts background training thread."""
        if self.worker_thread is not None and self.worker_thread.is_alive():
            return
        self.stop_event.clear()
        self.worker_thread = threading.Thread(target=self._worker_loop, daemon=True)
        self.worker_thread.start()

    def stop(self, timeout: float = 3.0) -> None:
        """Stops background training thread and joins."""
        if self.worker_thread is None:
            return
        self.stop_event.set()
        self.worker_thread.join(timeout=timeout)
        self.worker_thread = None

    def get_metrics(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Returns background trainer performance and loss summary."""
        with self.lock:
            # deque does not support slicing; materialize the bounded window first.
            recent_losses = list(self.loss_history)[-50:] if self.loss_history else []
            mean_loss = (
                float(np.mean([entry["loss"] for entry in recent_losses if "loss" in entry]))
                if recent_losses
                else 0.0
            )
            return {
                "training_steps": self.training_steps,
                # Retained window length (capped at loss_history_maxlen);
                # `training_steps` remains the uncapped total update count.
                "loss_history_len": len(self.loss_history),
                "loss_history_maxlen": self.loss_history_maxlen,
                "mean_recent_loss": round(mean_loss, 4),
                "consecutive_failed_swaps": self.consecutive_failed_swaps,
                "fatal_error": self.fatal_error,
                "hot_swap_stats": self.hot_swap_manager.get_stats(),
            }


class HotSwapRLScheduler:
    """
    S1/S2/S3 compliant RL scheduler that serves uplink grants using the fast Act model
    and streams retrospective transitions to the background trainer.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        act_model: nn.Module,
        hot_swap_manager: DualModelHotSwapManager,
        streamer: TransitionStreamer,
        vectorizer: Optional[StateVectorizer] = None,
        rsu_range: float = RSU_RANGE,
        decoder: Optional[ActionDecoder] = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.act_model = act_model
        self.hot_swap_manager = hot_swap_manager
        self.streamer = streamer
        self.vectorizer = vectorizer or StateVectorizer(rsu_range=rsu_range)
        # Single source of truth for the action ranges: src/rl_interface.py::ActionDecoder.
        self.decoder = decoder or ActionDecoder()
        # Observation width is read from the vectorizer, never hardcoded.
        self.state_dim = infer_state_dim(self.vectorizer)
        self.rsu_range = float(rsu_range)
        # The reward weights that used to live here (alpha_aoi / beta_error /
        # gamma_power) are gone. The scheduler does not price transitions any
        # more -- the environment owns the one reward function (design_spec_v2 P1).
        self.inference_latencies_ms: List[float] = []
        self.total_inferences = 0

    def decide_grant(
        self,
        vid: str,
        state_vec: np.ndarray,
    ) -> Tuple[Tuple[float, int, float], Any]:
        """Run the Act model on an observation the ENVIRONMENT produced.

        This method is pure inference. It used to also (a) build its own state
        vector from a partial dict and (b) compute its own three-term reward,
        which is what the replay buffer was actually trained on. Both are gone:

          (a) it re-vectorised from `{vid, current_time, pos, speed}`, so 15 of
              the 18 dimensions fell back to defaults and reached the model as
              constants -- traffic light, distance to RSU, CBR, heading, age.
              The rich vector the environment builds was discarded by the caller.
          (b) its reward was `-(0.1*dt + 1.0*err + 0.01*power)` with `err`
              permanently 0 (the key was never passed) and `dt` permanently 0.1,
              i.e. the only live training signal in the whole pipeline was
              transmit power. The approved four-term reward went to the log file.

        Both now have exactly one owner, the environment (design_spec_v2 P1/P2).

        Returns `(grant, raw_action, action_idx)`. The caller stores the last two
        so the transition can be pushed with the action the policy actually
        emitted AND with the discrete index its discrete head actually chose.

        The third element used to be dropped on the floor here: `select_action`
        returns `(grant, raw_action, info)` and `info["action_idx"]` is where the
        five discrete-head baselines report their argmax, so discarding it forced
        every one of them onto a lossy reconstruction path.
        """
        s = np.asarray(state_vec, dtype=np.float32)
        assert s.shape == (self.state_dim,), (
            f"FATAL: observation for {vid} has width {s.shape}, expected ({self.state_dim},). "
            "The environment is the only legitimate source of observations."
        )

        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        self.act_model.eval()
        with self.hot_swap_manager.swap_lock:
            grant, raw_action, info = self.act_model.select_action(s, deterministic=False)

        self.inference_latencies_ms.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000.0)
        self.total_inferences += 1

        action_idx: Optional[int] = None
        if isinstance(info, dict):
            raw_idx = info.get("action_idx")
            if raw_idx is not None:
                try:
                    action_idx = int(raw_idx)
                except (TypeError, ValueError):
                    action_idx = None
        return grant, raw_action, action_idx

    def push_transition(
        self,
        state: np.ndarray,
        raw_action: Any,
        reward: float,
        next_state: np.ndarray,
        done: bool,
        delta_t: float,
        action_idx: Optional[int] = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Stream one closed SMDP interval to the background trainer.

        `reward` and `delta_t` come from the environment: the reward is the
        four-term interval reward and `delta_t` is the MEASURED interval, which
        differs from the requested Delta whenever a failed uplink was retried.
        The buffer discounts by gamma**delta_t, so feeding it the requested value
        would misprice exactly the intervals that went wrong.
        """
        self.streamer.push(
            state=state,
            action=raw_action,
            reward=float(reward),
            next_state=next_state,
            done=bool(done),
            delta_t=float(delta_t),
            action_idx=action_idx,
        )


    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Resets per-episode state."""
        self.inference_latencies_ms.clear()

    def get_latency_stats(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """Returns serving inference latency percentiles in ms."""
        if not self.inference_latencies_ms:
            return {"mean_latency_ms": 0.0, "p50_latency_ms": 0.0, "p95_latency_ms": 0.0, "p99_latency_ms": 0.0}
        arr = np.array(self.inference_latencies_ms)
        return {
            "mean_latency_ms": round(float(np.mean(arr)), 4),
            "p50_latency_ms": round(float(np.percentile(arr, 50)), 4),
            "p95_latency_ms": round(float(np.percentile(arr, 95)), 4),
            "p99_latency_ms": round(float(np.percentile(arr, 99)), 4),
        }

    """
    Master Orchestrator for Dual-Model Hot-Swap Training.
    Manages Act model, Rest model, ReplayBuffer, Streamer, Worker, and Hot-Swap synchronization.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        model_name: Union[str, type, Callable] = "GenericPolicy",
        model_cls: Optional[Callable] = None,
        state_dim: Optional[int] = None,
        num_channels: int = 4,
        buffer_capacity: int = 10000,
        batch_size: int = 32,
        swap_interval: int = 20,
        act_device: Optional[Union[str, torch.device]] = None,
        rest_device: Optional[Union[str, torch.device]] = None,
        hparams: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    ) -> None:
        if model_cls is None:
            if callable(model_name) and not isinstance(model_name, str):
                model_cls = model_name
                self.model_name = getattr(model_cls, "__name__", "CustomModel")
            else:
                raise NotImplementedError(
                    f"Baseline models scraped. New IEEE baselines to be provided. Cannot instantiate '{model_name}' without model_cls."
                )
        else:
            self.model_name = str(model_name) if isinstance(model_name, str) else getattr(model_name, "__name__", "CustomModel")

        # `state_dim=None` (default) reads the width straight off StateVectorizer so
        # this orchestrator tracks the state layout automatically; an explicit int is
        # still honoured for backward compatibility.
        self.state_dim = int(state_dim) if state_dim is not None else infer_state_dim()
        self.num_channels = int(num_channels)
        self.buffer_capacity = int(buffer_capacity)
        self.batch_size = int(batch_size)
        self.swap_interval = int(swap_interval)

        # w1..w4 are AoiV2IEnv arguments, not model arguments. Every baseline
        # constructor ends in `**hparams`, so leaving them in here would have
        # them absorbed by the model and silently dropped from the reward --
        # exactly the failure this split exists to prevent.
        self.hparams, self.env_hparams = split_env_hparams(hparams)
        if self.env_hparams:
            logging.info(
                "%s: routed environment key(s) %s away from the model constructor. "
                "Reward weights come from DEFAULT_REWARD_WEIGHTS and are not tuned "
                "per model; the rest are handed to AoiV2IEnv by the caller.",
                self.model_name, sorted(self.env_hparams),
            )

        # Device Placement
        default_act_dev, default_rest_dev = select_default_devices()
        self.act_device = torch.device(act_device) if act_device is not None else default_act_dev
        self.rest_device = torch.device(rest_device) if rest_device is not None else default_rest_dev

        # Instantiate Models
        self.act_model = model_cls(state_dim=self.state_dim, num_channels=self.num_channels, **self.hparams).to(
            self.act_device
        )
        self.rest_model = model_cls(state_dim=self.state_dim, num_channels=self.num_channels, **self.hparams).to(
            self.rest_device
        )
        self._assert_model_consumed_hparams(self.act_model)

        self.act_model.eval()
        self.rest_model.train()

        # Shared synchronization & infrastructure
        self.swap_lock = threading.Lock()
        # Guards the Rest weights against readers while a gradient step mutates
        # them. Shared by the hot-swap manager and the background trainer so a
        # swap, a gradient step and a checkpoint write cannot interleave.
        self.update_lock = threading.Lock()
        self.hot_swap_manager = DualModelHotSwapManager(
            act_model=self.act_model,
            rest_model=self.rest_model,
            act_device=self.act_device,
            rest_device=self.rest_device,
            swap_lock=self.swap_lock,
            update_lock=self.update_lock,
        )

        # Initial weight sync (Rest -> Act). It is a synchronisation, not a
        # scheduled swap, so it is excluded from the count the paper reports.
        self.hot_swap_manager.hot_swap()
        self.hot_swap_manager.swap_count = 0

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # SMDP discount: ONE source, the model's own `gamma`.
        #
        # `RetrospectiveReplayBuffer` computes `discount = gamma ** delta_t` from
        # ITS OWN gamma and ships it in every batch. This buffer used to be built
        # without a gamma argument, so it always used its 0.99 default while the
        # per-model `gamma` that Optuna searched, recorded in the CSV and reported
        # as an optimum had no effect on learning in any of the nine baselines.
        # The buffer now takes the model's gamma, so the column it ships and the
        # value the model recomputes from `delta_t` are the same number.
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        self.gamma = float(
            getattr(self.rest_model, "gamma", self.hparams.get("gamma", 0.99))
        )
        self.replay_buffer = RetrospectiveReplayBuffer(
            capacity=self.buffer_capacity, gamma=self.gamma
        )
        self.streamer = TransitionStreamer(maxsize=self.buffer_capacity * 2)

        self.background_trainer = BackgroundTrainer(
            rest_model=self.rest_model,
            replay_buffer=self.replay_buffer,
            streamer=self.streamer,
            hot_swap_manager=self.hot_swap_manager,
            batch_size=self.batch_size,
            swap_interval_steps=self.swap_interval,
            rest_device=self.rest_device,

            act_model=self.act_model,
            hot_swap_manager=self.hot_swap_manager,

    def _assert_model_consumed_hparams(self, model: nn.Module) -> None:
        """Fail loudly when a hyper-parameter reached the model and did nothing.

        Every baseline `__init__` ends in `**hparams` and forwards the remainder
        up the chain; `BaseAgent.__init__` is the terminus and stores whatever is
        left on `self.hparams` purely so it can be written into the save file. So
        "the key is still sitting in `model.hparams`" is an EXACT test for "no
        constructor in the MRO named it, and it therefore had no effect" -- it
        covers the `super().__init__(**hparams)` chains and the SB3 wrappers'
        `**algo_kwargs` forwarding alike, which a signature whitelist on the leaf
        class cannot do without rejecting legitimate keys.

        This is an exception rather than a warning on purpose. The previous
        `logging.warning` was correct and useless: nobody reads a warning buried
        in an 8.8 hour log, and the run it warns about is exactly the run whose
        numbers must not be trusted.
        """
        leftovers = getattr(model, "hparams", None)
        if not isinstance(leftovers, dict):
            return
        unconsumed = sorted(k for k in self.hparams if k in leftovers)
        if unconsumed:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{self.model_name}: hyper-parameter(s) {unconsumed} reached the model "
                f"constructor but no `__init__` in its MRO names them, so they were "
                f"absorbed by the `**hparams` tail and had NO effect on training. "
                f"They are also not arguments of AoiV2IEnv ({sorted(env_param_names())}). "
                f"Fix the key name, or add it to the model's signature."

            "swap_count": self.hot_swap_manager.swap_count,

        """

        was_training = self.policy.training
        self.policy.set_training_mode(False)
        with torch.no_grad():
            actions, values, log_prob = self.policy(obs, deterministic=deterministic)
        self.policy.set_training_mode(was_training)

        raw_action = actions.detach().cpu().numpy().reshape(-1).astype(np.float32)
        grant = self.decode(raw_action)

            "log_prob": float(log_prob.detach().cpu().reshape(-1)[0]),

    def update(self, batch: Dict[str, torch.Tensor]) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """
        One PPO update treating the sampled batch as a single short rollout.

        See the module header for the on-policy/off-policy caveat this carries.
        Mirrors `stable_baselines3.PPO.train()` except that (a) the advantage
        comes from a 1-step SMDP TD target instead of GAE over a contiguous
        rollout, and (b) `old_log_prob` is a snapshot of the current policy
        rather than the true behaviour policy.
        """
        states, actions, rewards, next_states, dones, discounts = self.unpack_batch(batch)
        sb3 = self._sb3
        self.policy.set_training_mode(True)

        # SB3 stores clip_range/clip_range_vf as schedules over the remaining
        # progress; our loop has no global progress signal, so evaluate at 1.0
        # (the constant-schedule case returns the configured value).
        clip_range = float(sb3.clip_range(1.0))
        clip_range_vf = float(sb3.clip_range_vf(1.0)) if sb3.clip_range_vf is not None else None

        with torch.no_grad():
            old_values = self.policy.predict_values(states).reshape(-1, 1)
            next_values = self.policy.predict_values(next_states).reshape(-1, 1)
            # lambda = 0 GAE: the buffer holds independent SMDP transitions, so a
            # multi-step advantage cannot be formed. gamma**delta_t comes per-sample.
            returns = rewards + (1.0 - dones) * discounts * next_values
            advantages = returns - old_values
            _, old_log_prob, _ = self.policy.evaluate_actions(states, actions)
            old_log_prob = old_log_prob.detach()

        n_epochs = int(sb3.n_epochs)
        pg_losses: List[float] = []
        value_losses: List[float] = []
        entropy_losses: List[float] = []
        clip_fractions: List[float] = []
        approx_kls: List[float] = []

        epochs_run = 0

            values, log_prob, entropy = self.policy.evaluate_actions(states, actions)
            values = values.reshape(-1, 1)

            adv = advantages
            if sb3.normalize_advantage and adv.shape[0] > 1:
                adv = (adv - adv.mean()) / (adv.std() + 1e-8)

            ratio = torch.exp(log_prob.reshape(-1, 1) - old_log_prob.reshape(-1, 1))

            policy_loss_2 = adv * torch.clamp(ratio, 1.0 - clip_range, 1.0 + clip_range)

            # the update even though it cannot bind against the behaviour policy.
            if sb3.target_kl is not None and approx_kl > 1.5 * float(sb3.target_kl):
                break

## Invalid Parameters

When validation is enabled and a parameter is invalid (such as containing NaN values), the distribution will reject it based on the `arg_constraints` property. ## Managing Validation

You can control validation behavior using the static method `set_default_validate_args(value)`. This method "sets whether validation is enabled or disabled," allowing you to override the default. The documentation notes that "validation may be expensive, so you may want to disable it once a model is working."

This approach lets you catch parameter errors during development while disabling the overhead in production once your code is verified.

## 1. 전수 스캔의 실측 근거

### 1.1 PPO는 두 팔 모두 학습 스레드가 죽었다

`runs/accumulate_seed42/sup/train.log:142`와 `runs/mean_seed42/sup/train.log:80`에 각각 한 번씩 `Exception in thread Thread-2 (_worker_loop)`가 남아 있다. 두 로그의 트레이스백은 같은 경로를 가리킨다. `src/hot_swap_trainer.py:674`의 `_worker_loop`가 `train_step`을 호출하고, `:631`에서 `self.rest_model.update(batch)`가 `src/baselines/sb3_ppo.py:188`의 `self.policy.evaluate_actions(states, actions)`로 들어가며, SB3의 `DiagGaussianDistribution.proba_distribution`이 `Normal(mean_actions, action_std)`를 만들 때 torch가 `ValueError: Expected parameter loc ... to satisfy the constraint Real(), but found invalid values: tensor([[nan, nan, nan], ...], device='cuda:1')`로 거부한다. 실패한 것은 스케일이 아니라 평균 헤드이고, 디바이스가 `cuda:1`이므로 죽은 것은 Rest 모델이다.

`_worker_loop`에는 예외 처리가 없다. 따라서 스레드는 그 자리에서 종료되고 이후 `train_step`이 다시 호출되지 않는다. 이것이 `grad_updates_total`이 accumulate 팔에서 1,610, mean 팔에서 746에 고정되고 `swap_count`가 각각 80과 37에서 멈춘 이유다. `consecutive_failed_swaps`는 `train_step` 안에서만 증가하므로(`src/hot_swap_trainer.py:638-656`) 스레드가 죽은 뒤에는 영원히 0에 머문다. 즉 `fatal_error` 경보(`:3217`)는 원리적으로 발동할 수 없었고, PPO 두 실행은 "실패로 중단된 모델이 없다"는 겉모습을 유지한 채 81개와 89개 에피소드를 갱신 0회로 완주했다. `Hot-swap REFUSED` 로그는 두 팔 어디에도 한 줄도 없다.

`mean_loss`가 발산 이후 소수점까지 똑같은 값으로 반복되는 것도 같은 원인이다. 이 열은 `get_metrics()`의 `mean_recent_loss`, 곧 최근 50개 손실의 평균인데(`:700-705`) 링 버퍼에 새 항목이 들어오지 않으니 값이 그대로 얼어붙는다. accumulate 팔의 16105591.1208이 ep19부터 ep100까지 82회 반복되는 것은 발산이 계속된 증거가 아니라 학습이 멈춘 증거다.

발산 자체는 스레드 사망보다 먼저 시작됐다. accumulate 팔은 ep16까지 손실 28.4782였다가 ep17에서 7,647,842.29로 뛰었고, mean 팔은 ep10까지 0.8827이었다가 ep11에서 285,247.46으로 뛰었다. 두 경우 모두 폭발과 NaN 사이에 두 에피소드 정도의 간격만 있었다.

동결된 Act 정책의 행동도 확인된다. accumulate 팔 PPO의 `mean_delta`는 밀도 5 에피소드 기준 ep15에서 3.4549초였으나 ep22에서 0.8881초, ep29에서 0.6171초로 내려앉았고 그 구간의 `reward_per_sec_selected`는 -0.270691에서 -0.586231, -0.859955로 악화된다. `DELTA_MIN`이 0.1초(`src/rl_interface.py:45`)이므로 정책은 사실상 최소 간격을 연발하는 축퇴 상태로 굳었다. 다만 이 세 에피소드는 모두 동결 이후이므로 정책 변화가 아니라 시나리오 차이일 여지가 있고, 확정적으로 말할 수 있는 것은 ep15와 ep22 사이 구간에서 Δ가 붕괴했다는 사실까지다.

### 1.2 I-HAMAPPO는 NaN 없이 발산했다. 가장 위험한 경우다

이쪽은 PPO와 달리 갱신이 끝까지 계속됐다. accumulate 팔은 44,580회, mean 팔은 25,210회 갱신했고 핫스왑도 각각 2,229회와 1,260회 정상 수행됐다. 경고는 한 줄도 뜨지 않았다. 그럼에도 손실은 완전히 무너져 있다.

accumulate 팔의 손실 궤적은 ep3에서 1.8072, ep4에서 16,384.98, ep6에서 10,339.84, ep10에서 543,955.21, ep13에서 10,368,102.85이고 그 뒤로는 ep100의 45,199,924.33까지 1e7에서 9.5e7 사이를 오간다. 보상도 같이 무너졌다. ep1의 -0.086705가 ep20 이후에는 -0.24에서 -0.28 대역에 고착되어 세 배 가까이 악화됐고, `_best.pt`는 갱신 132회 시점인 ep1에 저장된 뒤 한 번도 갱신되지 않았다.

mean 팔은 더 교묘하다. 손실은 ep7에서 21.9171, ep16에서 145,990.14, ep34에서 462,900.36으로 튀었다가 ep38 이후 1e6에서 5.4e7 사이에 눌러앉는다. 그런데 `reward_per_sec_selected`는 -0.0037에서 -0.0068 사이를 유지해 SAC(-0.0034)나 TD3(-0.0040)와 구별되지 않는다. 그리고 `_best.pt`는 ep85에 저장됐는데 그 에피소드의 `mean_loss`는 16,520,319.66이다. 즉 논문 표에 들어갈 I-HAMAPPO mean 정책은 크리틱이 완전히 발산한 상태에서 학습된 액터다.

메커니즘은 코드에서 확인된다. `src/baselines/i_hamappo.py:404`의 반환 딕셔너리에서 `loss`는 `actor_loss + value_coef * value_loss`인데, 액터 항은 클리핑된 대리 목적(`:382-385`)과 정규화된 어드밴티지(`:370-374`), 그리고 `grad_clip`(`:392`)으로 O(1) 범위에 묶여 있다. 따라서 1e7 규모는 전적으로 `value_loss`에서 온다. 크리틱이 발산하면 `advantages = target_v - v_pred.detach()`(`:360`)의 부호가 잡음에 지배되고, 정규화를 거쳐도 크기만 O(1)이 될 뿐 방향은 무의미해진다. 액터는 계속 갱신되지만 무엇을 향해 갱신되는지는 보장되지 않는다.

### 1.3 나머지 일곱 모델은 발산하지 않았다

SAC, TD3, RES-MAPDDPG, MA2HDQN, SPAM-D3QN, CARLTON, MADDPG-MT의 열네 실행 전부에서 `grad_updates_this_episode`가 0인 에피소드는 하나도 없고, `mean_loss`는 단조 감소하거나 좁은 대역에서 진동한다. 최종값 기준으로 SPAM-D3QN mean이 0.0005로 가장 낮고 CARLTON accumulate가 1.1139로 가장 높으며, 어느 것도 발산 추세를 보이지 않는다. `swap_count`도 갱신 수에 비례해 끝까지 증가한다.

### 1.4 CARLTON은 발산이 아니라 정체다

CARLTON mean 실행은 100 에피소드 동안 `reward_per_sec_selected`가 -0.021095에서 -0.025484 사이에만 머문다. 문제는 값의 크기가 아니라 밀도 반응이 없다는 점이다. 다른 여덟 모델은 밀도 5 에피소드에서 밀도 25~35 에피소드보다 서너 배 좋은 점수를 내는데, CARLTON mean은 밀도와 무관하게 같은 값을 낸다. 행동을 직접 보면 원인이 분명하다. `mean_delta`가 ep1에서 10.5528초, ep14에서 10.7500초, ep92에서 10.7219초, ep100에서 10.5379초로 43,526회 갱신 내내 사실상 상수다. 같은 팔의 SAC는 ep92~ep100 구간에서 밀도 5에 25.2초, 밀도 25~35에 19.0~19.6초로 밀도에 따라 Δ를 조절한다. CARLTON mean의 정책은 초기값에서 움직이지 않았다고 보는 것이 자연스럽다.

accumulate 팔은 사정이 다르다. `mean_delta`가 ep1의 10.516초에서 ep7까지 6.69초로 내려간 뒤 ep99의 6.2759초까지 그대로 유지된다. 초기 7 에피소드에서 한 번 움직인 뒤 93 에피소드 동안 정지한 셈이다. 다만 같은 밀도끼리 비교하면 밀도 5 기준 ep1의 -0.153055가 ep99에서 -0.097734로 36퍼센트 개선되었으므로 학습이 전혀 없었다고 단정할 수는 없다.

| I-HAMAPPO mean | ep5 (0.0237) | ep7 (21.9171) | 10,000 ~ 14,000 | 775 ~ 5,481 |

여기서 팀 리드의 전제를 하나 수정해야 한다. HPO 롤아웃은 "350스텝에 학습 2회"가 아니다. `src/hpo.py:466-468`을 보면 버퍼가 16개 이상 찬 뒤로는 매 환경 스텝마다 `train_steps_during_rollout=2`(`:608`)회씩 갱신하므로, 350스텝 롤아웃(`:663`) 하나당 최대 약 700회의 그래디언트 갱신이 일어난다. 그리고 이것이 문제의 핵심이다. PPO mean은 갱신 746회 지점에서 발산했다. HPO의 탐색 지평이 그 바로 앞에서 끊긴다.

따라서 필요한 롤아웃 연장 배수는 다음과 같이 계산된다. 갱신 횟수 기준으로 PPO mean은 약 1.1배, I-HAMAPPO accumulate는 약 3배, PPO accumulate는 약 2.2배만 늘려도 발산이 관측 범위에 들어온다. 환경 스텝 기준으로 보면 훨씬 길어서, I-HAMAPPO accumulate는 8,000스텝으로 약 23배, PPO mean은 22,000스텝으로 약 63배가 필요하다. 두 기준이 크게 어긋나는 이유는 본훈련의 백그라운드 트레이너가 `train_frequency`로 스텝당 갱신 비율을 제한하는데(`src/hot_swap_trainer.py:660-669`) HPO 롤아웃은 스텝당 무조건 2회를 돌기 때문이다. 어느 쪽을 맞출 것인지가 설계 결정 사항이라 아래 질문 절에 올린다.

부수적으로 확인한 사실이 하나 더 있다. `src/hpo.py:469-483`에서 `model.update()`의 예외는 잡혀서 `n_update_failures`로 집계될 뿐 트라이얼을 실패시키지 않는다. 다행히 PPO와 I-HAMAPPO 두 스터디 모두 `user_attrs_n_update_failures`가 전 트라이얼 0이므로 HPO 도중에 NaN이 난 적은 없다. 그러나 PPO 스터디의 15 트라이얼 중 다섯 개(번호 0, 2, 6, 7, 14)는 `n_failed_seeds=3`, `n_observations=-1`로 아무것도 측정하지 못한 채 벌점 100.0을 받았고, 이 다섯 개의 학습률은 각각 7.66e-4, 1.44e-3, 2.87e-3, 1.88e-3, 2.36e-3으로 전부 상위 구간이다. 살아남은 최고 트라이얼 10의 학습률 1.08e-3은 그 바로 아래 경계에 있다. 실패 원인을 CSV만으로는 특정할 수 없으므로 상관관계로만 기록한다.

| 모델 | 학습률 | gamma | 발산 여부 |
|---|---|---|---|
| PPO | 1.0809e-3 (ent_coef 2.051e-2, n_epochs 4) | 0.9975073 | 발산 |
| I-HAMAPPO | actor 8.433e-4 / critic 5.608e-4 (entropy_coef 4.483e-3) | 0.9986278 | 발산 |
| SAC | 2.7207e-3 | 0.9728362 | 정상 |
| TD3 | 1.4286e-4 | 0.9686211 | 정상 |
| RES-MAPDDPG | actor 1.0371e-4 / critic 3.0387e-4 | 0.9503075 | 정상 |
| MA2HDQN | q 1.3304e-3 / actor 3.339e-4 / critic 1.0117e-4 | 0.9610090 | 정상 |
| SPAM-D3QN | 3.4766e-4 | 0.9723474 | 정상 |
| CARLTON | 1.0511e-4 | 0.9722837 | 정상 |
| MADDPG-MT | actor 7.661e-4 / critic 1.700e-4 | 0.9576437 | 진행 중, 정상 |

가장 깨끗한 상관은 학습률이 아니라 gamma다. 발산한 두 모델의 gamma는 0.9975와 0.99863으로 아홉 중 1위와 2위이고, 정상인 일곱 모델은 전부 0.9503에서 0.9728 구간에 있다. 두 집합 사이에 겹침이 없다. 학습률만으로는 설명되지 않는데, SAC가 2.72e-3으로 PPO보다 2.5배 높은 학습률을 받고도 멀쩡하기 때문이다. gamma가 결정적인 이유는 이 프로젝트가 SMDP 할인 `gamma ** delta_t`를 쓰고(`src/hot_swap_trainer.py:943-956`) 두 발산 모델 모두 1스텝 TD 부트스트랩으로 가치 목표를 만들기 때문이다. `src/baselines/sb3_ppo.py:186`의 `returns = rewards + (1.0 - dones) * discounts * next_values`와 `src/baselines/i_hamappo.py:345`의 `value_loss = F.mse_loss(v_pred, target_v)`가 그것이다. gamma가 1에 가까울수록 부트스트랩 되먹임의 수축률이 1에 붙고 1/(1-gamma) 항이 폭발한다.

I-HAMAPPO의 경우 HPO가 gamma를 1 쪽으로 몬 흔적이 트라이얼 CSV에 그대로 남아 있다. `results/hpo/optuna_trials_I-HAMAPPO.csv`에서 점수 상위 세 트라이얼은 11번(16.29, gamma 0.99863), 12번(16.99, gamma 0.99895), 5번(17.38, gamma 0.99751)이고 셋 다 gamma가 0.9975를 넘는다. 같은 세 트라이얼의 `tx_attempts`는 867, 1385, 632로 전체에서 가장 높다. 350스텝짜리 짧은 롤아웃에서는 전송을 많이 할수록 AoI와 오차가 좋아 보이므로 목적함수가 짧은 Δ와 긴 지평을 동시에 상으로 준 셈인데, 두 성질 모두 20만 스텝에서는 손해로 돌아온다.

### 문헌 대비 통상값

SB3 공식 문서에 기재된 PPO 생성자 기본값은 `learning_rate=0.0003`, `gamma=0.99`, `ent_coef=0.0`, `vf_coef=0.5`, `max_grad_norm=0.5`, `target_kl=None`이다. 이 프로젝트의 PPO 학습률 1.08e-3은 기본값의 3.6배다. RL Baselines3 Zoo가 공개한 연속 제어 환경별 튜닝값을 보면 HalfCheetah-v4가 2.06e-5, Walker2d-v4가 5.05e-5, Hopper-v4가 9.81e-5, BipedalWalker-v3가 3e-4이고 가장 높은 축인 Pendulum-v1이 1e-3이다. 다시 말해 1.08e-3은 공개된 튜닝값 분포의 최상단을 넘어선다. 엔트로피 계수는 격차가 더 크다. Zoo의 연속 제어 값들은 0.0에서 4.29e-3 사이에 있는데 이 프로젝트의 PPO는 2.051e-2로 최댓값의 약 다섯 배다. SAC와 TD3의 SB3 기본값은 각각 3e-4와 1e-3, gamma는 둘 다 0.99, tau는 0.005다. 이 기준으로 보면 SAC의 2.72e-3은 기본값의 9배로 상당히 공격적이지만 실제로는 발산하지 않았고, TD3의 1.43e-4는 기본값의 7분의 1로 보수적이다.

엔트로피 계수를 눈여겨봐야 하는 이유가 하나 더 있다. 로컬 SB3 설치본 `/home/imnyj/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/stable_baselines3/common/distributions.py:150`에서 `log_std`는 아무 제약 없는 자유 파라미터이고 `:163`의 `action_std = th.ones_like(mean_actions) * log_std.exp()`에도 클램프가 없다. 가우시안 엔트로피는 위로 유계가 아니므로 엔트로피 보너스는 `log_std`를 무한정 밀어올릴 수 있고, 이를 막는 것은 정책 손실뿐이다. 다만 이번 트레이스백에서 NaN이 난 것은 스케일이 아니라 평균(`loc`)이므로 이 경로가 실제 원인이라고 단정하지는 않는다. 검증 가능한 가설로만 남긴다.

## 4. Act 모델의 유효성

`_best.pt`는 `ep_reward_per_sec > best_reward`일 때만 다시 쓰이므로(`src/hot_swap_trainer.py:3253-3256`) 각 실행의 최고 보상 에피소드가 곧 그 파일의 나이다. 18개 파일이 모두 디스크에 존재하는 것은 확인했다. 위 판정표의 best 에피소드 열이 그대로 각 `_best.pt`의 정체이며, 특히 주의할 것은 다음 네 건이다.

PPO accumulate의 `_best.pt`는 ep1, 곧 갱신 40회짜리 정책이다. TD3 같은 팔의 59,156회와 비교하면 1,479분의 1이다. I-HAMAPPO accumulate의 `_best.pt`는 ep1, 갱신 132회다. 이 둘은 "100 에피소드를 훈련했다"고 표에 적을 수 없다. PPO mean은 ep8, 갱신 508회로 그나마 발산 이전이지만 여전히 다른 모델의 40분의 1 수준이다. I-HAMAPPO mean은 ep85로 갱신 횟수 자체는 22,638회로 충분하지만 그 시점의 손실이 1.65e7이므로 발산 이후의 정책이다.

한편 정상 모델 중에서도 RES-MAPDDPG mean은 별도 표기가 필요하다. `_best.pt`가 ep15, 갱신 4,122회 시점의 정책인데 실행 자체는 19,687회까지 갔다. 즉 이 모델은 15 에피소드 이후 100 에피소드까지 한 번도 자기 최고 기록을 넘지 못했다. 발산은 아니지만 조기 정체이므로, 100 에피소드를 돌렸다는 서술과 실제로 쓰이는 정책의 나이가 다르다는 점은 논문에 반영되어야 한다.

여기에 선택 지표 자체의 편향도 겹친다. `reward_per_sec_selected`는 밀도가 낮을수록 좋게 나오는데(예: SAC mean은 밀도 5에서 -0.0035, 밀도 35에서 -0.0058) 밀도 스케줄이 순환하므로 최고 기록은 거의 항상 밀도 5 또는 10 에피소드에서 나온다. 실제로 열여덟 실행의 best 에피소드 중 열넷이 밀도 5 에피소드이고 나머지도 밀도 10이다. 결과적으로 `_best.pt`는 "가장 잘 학습된 정책"이 아니라 "가장 쉬운 밀도를 뽑은 정책"에 가깝다. 이것은 발산과 별개의 구조적 문제이므로 아래 질문 절에 함께 올린다.

## 7. 담당 에이전트별 수정 지침

`p4-coder`에게. 첫째, `BackgroundTrainer._worker_loop`(`src/hot_swap_trainer.py:671-678`)에 예외 처리를 넣어 `train_step`이 던진 예외를 `fatal_error`로 승격시켜야 한다. 지금 구조에서는 스레드가 죽어도 아무도 모르고 나머지 8시간이 그대로 소모된다. 둘째, 갱신이 연속으로 0회인 에피소드가 일정 수를 넘으면 실행을 중단해야 한다. `zero_update_episodes` 카운터는 이미 있으나(`:3186-3192`) 경고만 남기고 중단하지 않는다. 셋째, `mean_loss`가 직전 창 대비 임계 배수 이상 뛰면 경보를 남기는 감시가 필요하다. I-HAMAPPO는 NaN에 닿지 않아 기존 어떤 가드에도 걸리지 않았다. 넷째, PPO와 I-HAMAPPO 두 모델의 크리틱 목표에 클리핑이나 정규화가 필요하다. 이 셋을 손대되 안티모킹 단언 4종과 `python -O` 거부 가드는 건드리지 말 것. 다섯째, `torch.distributions`의 인자 검증을 끄는 방식(`Distribution.set_default_validate_args(False)`)으로 이번 예외를 우회하면 NaN이 조용히 Act 모델까지 흘러가므로 절대 채택하면 안 된다. 지금은 이 검증이 유일하게 작동한 방어선이었다.

`p4-writer`에게. PPO 두 실행과 I-HAMAPPO 두 실행의 숫자는 어떤 형태로도 본문이나 표에 쓸 수 없다. 재훈련 결과가 나오기 전까지는 해당 칸을 비워 두고, 만약 발산 사실 자체를 논문에 서술한다면 위 2절의 실측 발산 시점과 3절의 gamma 대비 표를 근거로 쓸 것. 또한 어느 모델이든 "100 에피소드, 20만 스텝 학습"이라고 쓸 때는 실제로 채점되는 정책이 몇 번째 에피소드의 것인지를 4절 표에서 확인하고 쓸 것. RES-MAPDDPG mean처럼 15번째 에피소드 정책이 채점되는 사례가 있다.
